searchText: I don't have a strong opinion on using a bitlist for pre-selecting bids. Seems a bit unnecessary if not enforced (maybe social layer enforcement is enough though), so, idk. Including proofs of equivocations, e.g. signed IL.txs_root(s), should be done, imo. Otherwise we'd have accept a 2x in worst-case bandwidth consumption (2 ILs/peer traveling the whole network), as well as another 2x in compute for builders (using ILs with different frame txs when equivocating - safe-playing builders will simulate them both) I'll be opening a PR that enforces bitlist inclusivity before next breakout so we can discuss it better. We've been focusing on something else that were needed to launch a devnet, but hopefully get to make a decision on the bitlist enforcement soon. Thanks to your input, I started to think that maybe having IL roots in a bid is the best way forward, especially given that the fact that it declares the superset IL view that a payload should be checked against. I think it's helpful for liveness even when the network is healthy. Oh yeah the issue of grieving the builders and creating a market for the IL so that I can include my own txs that I know I can invalidate, I haven't seen a solution for that. That is with honest but rational includers. If I also get them to equivocate then the grievance to my competition is even worse
